# LiteracyLab AI

> LiteracyLab AI is an AI-powered literacy coach for students aged 5-18. It reads a child's writing, or checks their reading comprehension, and returns feedback cited against that child's own country's real school curriculum — not generic writing advice.

## What it does

- Generates an original writing prompt or reading-comprehension passage suited to the student's age tier and stated interests (e.g. space, gaming, history).
- Grades the submission and returns structured feedback: one "Glow" (a specific strength, tied to a named curriculum standard), one "Grow" (a single actionable next step, explained through the student's own interest), and two vocabulary upgrades, each with a usage example.
- Teaches a named writing framework alongside every writing piece — Show Don't Tell, Story Mountain, PEEL or PEAL, matched to the genre of that specific piece rather than fixed by age — with a fresh worked example demonstrating it, not just the name.
- For writing, also shows the student's own story rewritten with the suggested improvement spliced directly into their original text ("Your story, revised"), rather than describing the fix only in the abstract.
- Scores every writing submission 1-10 against the whole piece (ideas, structure, language, technical accuracy), independently of the single coached "Grow" above, so the score stays honest even when the coaching stays narrow.
- Builds a vocabulary bank from every word a learner has been taught, with a multiple-choice self-test quiz once they've learned at least 4 words.
- Tracks mastery over time against real, named curriculum targets on a parent-facing dashboard, including a weekly progress trend and an anonymous comparison against other students in the same country and grade/year.

## Who it's for

Parents and guardians of students aged 5-18, across four age-tiered workspaces (Early Years, Elementary, Middle School, High School). Every account is created and managed by a parent or guardian; children do not register independently.

## Curricula supported

UK National Curriculum / GCSE, US Common Core / AP, Australia ACARA, Canada provincial standards, UAE & GCC (Cambridge/IGCSE), Singapore & SE Asia (Cambridge/IB), and a CEFR-aligned Global ESL mode (A1-C2) for learners anywhere else.

## Parent guides

Plain-English guides to what children learn in reading and writing, year by year, for each supported region (UK, US, Australia, Canada, UAE & Gulf, Singapore & South-East Asia, and CEFR levels for English learners): https://www.literacylabai.com/learn/

## Pricing

- Free: 3 writing or reading submissions per calendar month, with full feedback (no watered-down free tier).
- Core: 9.99/month in the customer's local currency (A$, US$, £, €, C$ or S$; US$ everywhere else) for one learner — unlimited submissions, a 26-week progress trend chart, anonymous ranking within their own year group, and full activity history.
- Premium: 15.99/month in the same local currency — everything in Core for up to 6 learners on one account, plus extended feedback (a second, harder next step on every piece) and exam-technique scoring for students aged 11+, which bands each piece 1-4 against the real assessment objectives published for their year and region, with evidence quoted from their own work. It never produces a raw exam mark, percentage or grade letter.

Both paid plans are billed monthly through Stripe with no lock-in contract; cancel anytime and the account drops back to the free plan.

## Privacy and safety

Parent-managed accounts by design. Student writing is processed only to generate feedback for that child — never sold, never used to train public AI models. Parents can review, export, or permanently delete a child's data at any time from the dashboard.

## Articles for parents

Plain-English explainers, each with FAQs: https://www.literacylabai.com/learn/articles/ — topics include KS2 SATs, 11+ and GCSE English Language, NAPLAN reading and writing, Common Core writing standards, PEEL/PEAL paragraphs, RACE and CER short answers, Show Don't Tell, Story Mountain, inference questions, reading poetry, building vocabulary, and correcting a child's writing without putting them off.

## Free printable worksheets

Original reading-comprehension worksheets with answer keys for the UK, US and Australia, written in each country's spelling and curriculum language: https://www.literacylabai.com/learn/worksheets/
